title: Unified Inference — Q2 2028: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Emily Carter
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, design notes, roadmap themes for Q2 2028, pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product family. It is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams.

High-level summary
- Product: Unified Inference (hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
- Q2 2028 focus: stability and cost-efficiency at scale, model routing improvements, and unified pricing tiers to simplify enterprise procurement.
- Outcome goals: 20% reduction in per-token unit cost for common web workloads, <= 50ms P50 latency for short-request tier, simplified packaging for mid-market customers.

1) Goals and success metrics
- Business goals:
  1. Enable predictable consumption with simplified pricing tiers for 80% of new seats.
  2. Accelerate Dedicated and Private bookings by providing clear migration path and TCO comparisons.
- Product/technical success metrics (tracked in product analytics and Console dashboards):
  - Unit-cost improvement: 20% reduction in average per-token cost for typical chat workloads (measured month-over-month).
  - Latency SLOs: P50 <= 50ms and P95 <= 200ms for the Short Request Tier (<= 256 tokens).
  - Stability: < 0.3% request error rate platform-wide attributable to runtime regressions.
  - Adoption: 30% of self-serve signups use new pricing tiers within 60 days of release.

2) Product Requirements (PRD) — core items
- User stories (top-level):
  - As an app developer, I want a single API surface with predictable latency and cost so I can choose a tier that matches my SLA and budget.
  - As an enterprise platform engineer, I want clear deployment and migration guides from Hosted to Dedicated to Private so I can maintain regulatory controls while reducing latency.
  - As a finance manager, I want packaged pricing with a TCO calculator to evaluate Dedicated commitments vs hosted usage.

- Functional requirements:
  - R1: Tiered offering with three tiers (Short, Standard, Long) mapped to latency & token budget. Each tier must have explicit batching and caching presets.
  - R2: Model routing policy engine that selects model variant based on policy (latency-first, cost-first, region affinity).
  - R3: Pricing API and SKU catalog that returns estimated monthly costs given usage patterns; integrates with Console cost estimators.
  - R4: Migration CLI and runbook for moving workloads from hosted to Dedicated/Private with automated canary and rollback.
  - R5: Telemetry hooks in runtime to emit per-request token counts, kernel selection, and batch membership.

- Non-functional requirements:
  - NFR1: Backwards-compatible API with deprecation notices (90-day window) for any breaking change.
  - NFR2: Security and compliance: must meet SOC2 controls already in place for Unified Inference. Private deployments must support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
  - NFR3: Performance: default configurations must meet SLOs in 99% of common production traffic shapes (based on March 2028 workload profile).

Requirements table (high-level)
| ID | Title | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| R1 | Tiered offering (Short/Standard/Long) | High | Product | Console displays three tiers; API returns tier attribution per request |
| R2 | Model routing policy engine | High | Eng - Serving Runtime | Policies can be configured per-customer and tested in canary; automated fallback works under capacity constraints |
| R3 | Pricing API & SKU catalog | Medium | Product/Finance | SKU catalog exposed via API; Console estimator returns an expected monthly cost given historical usage |
| R4 | Migration CLI & runbook | Medium | Eng - Private Deployments | CLI automates canary deploys; runbook validated in two pilot customers |
| R5 | Telemetry hooks | High | Eng - Platform | Events emitted to observability backend with <1s processing lag and visible in Console tracing |

3) Design specs and implementation notes
- Architecture overview (summary)
  - The Unified Inference control plane will continue to be hosted. Key additions for Q2: policy-driven model router, tier-aware batching layer, and pricing API.
  - Runtime will expose a routing decision API (internal) that uses tenant policies and recent latency/cost signals to choose a model variant.

- Design constraints and trade-offs
  - We prioritize predictable latency for the Short tier; this limits batching opportunities at the lowest latency but reduces tail variance.
  - Cost-optimized routing will use quantized model variants; ensure quality guardrails via evals and A/B holdback.

- Key components (owner hints):
  - Routing service (eng-serving-runtime): decision logs, policy store, health signals.
  - Tiered batching layer (eng-serving-runtime): config per tier, dynamic batch size limits.
  - Pricing API (eng-platform + finance): SKU service, estimator.
  - Migration tooling (eng-private-deployments): CLI + runbook + test harness.

Design snippets
- Example policy JSON (console-visible)
```json
{
  "policy_id": "policy-short-latency",
  "priority": "latency",
  "tier": "short",
  "model_preferences": ["gptx-small-q4", "gptx-small-fp16"],
  "fallback": "gptx-micro",
  "max_batch_ms": 10
}
```

- Console estimator CLI example
```
$ redwood pricing estimate --sku short-tier --monthly-requests 1000000 --avg-tokens 60
Estimated monthly cost: $6,400 (hosted)
Estimated monthly cost: $3,500 (dedicated, committed)
```

4) Roadmap & themes — Q2 2028
- Themes:
  - Theme A: Predictable performance (tier SLOs, short-tier optimization)
  - Theme B: Cost efficiency (routing, batching, quantization guidelines)
  - Theme C: Enterprise readiness (pricing clarity, migration path, Private packaging)

- Quarter milestones:
  - April 2028: M1 — Tiered offering shipped to Console beta; pricing SKU catalog published; initial routing service MVP.
  - May 2028: M2 — Tier-aware batching released to hosted customers; two pilot Dedicated migrations completed.
  - June 2028: M3 — Pricing API GA; migration CLI and Private runbook published; release notes and customer-facing docs live.

5) Pricing and packaging notes
- Simplified tiering (recommended public):
  - Short Tier: optimized for low-latency short requests (<=256 tokens). Price: $0.0027 per 1k tokens (example list price).
  - Standard Tier: balanced latency/cost for typical chat workloads. Price: $0.0018 per 1k tokens.
  - Long Tier: for long-context workloads (>2048 tokens), optimized for throughput. Price: $0.0012 per 1k tokens.
- Dedicated/Private packaging guidance:
  - Dedicated: monthly commit with instance-based SKUs and optional burst pool. Provide a TCO calculator comparing committed vs hosted.
  - Private: platform fee + per-GPU compute licensing; additional professional services for on-prem packaging and validation.
- Discounts and enterprise terms:
  - Committed usage discounts: 15-40% depending on term and minimums.
  - Volume-based overage tiers and negotiated ingress/outbound networking allowances for Private.

6) Release notes — Q2 2028 (v2028.2)
- GA features (June 2028):
  - Pricing API and SKU catalog (GA).
  - Migration CLI and validated runbook for Dedicated/Private migrations.
  - Tier-aware batching default presets for Short/Standard/Long tiers.
  - Console: new Pricing Estimator, TCO comparison view, and per-tenant routing policy editor.

- Beta / early access (April- May 2028):
  - Routing policy engine (beta) with canary testing.
  - Short-tier optimizations (experimental kernels) available to pilot customers.

- Deprecations / breaking changes
  - No breaking API changes in this release. Any small deprecations announced with 90-day windows.

7) Rollout plan and risk mitigations
- Staged rollout:
  1. Internal dogfooding (2 weeks) — validate telemetry and Console UX.
  2. Pilot cohort (3 customers, 3-6 weeks) — test migration CLI and routing policy defaults.
  3. Gradual public opt-in (4-6 weeks) — open Short/Standard/Long tiers in Console and enable Pricing API.

- Risk mitigations:
  - Observability: add targeted dashboards (per-tier latency, batch size, kernel selection) before public opt-in.
  - Fallbacks: routing engine supports immediate fallback to a compatible model variant and region.
  - Quality guardrails: A/B holdback for quantized variants and automatic regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

8) Ownership, dependencies, and next steps
- Primary owners:
  - Product (Emily Carter) — overall release and pricing coordination.
  - Eng - Serving Runtime (Raj Patel) — routing engine and tiered batching.
  - Eng - Platform (Sofia Martinez) — Pricing API, Console changes, telemetry.
  - Eng - Private Deployments (Liam O'Connor) — migration CLI, runbooks, on-prem packaging.

- Dependencies:
  - Kernel selection improvements (eng-serving-runtime) for short-tier performance.
  - Finance and legal sign-off on SKU language and enterprise contract templates.
  - Customer success readiness and updated playbooks for migration support.

- Immediate next steps (owner + ETA):
  1. Finalize SKU language with Finance (Product — 2028-04-01).
  2. Complete routing policy beta tests and add decision logging (Eng - Serving Runtime — 2028-04-22).
  3. Publish Console Pricing Estimator beta (Eng - Platform — 2028-05-06).
